title: Pawn breakthrough: sell two pawns, promote the third

difficulty.label: Club player who must recognise the breakthrough shape before the defending king arrives

objective.summary: Three pawns abreast against two, kings far from the queening square. The win is a forced sale: two pawns are given away so the outside pawn runs through unopposed. Order is everything — the wrong first pawn seals the front and the tablebase calls it a draw. Break through, promote, win.

planClasses.label: Break through the fixed front
planClasses.description: Sacrifice into the majority so one runner emerges past the defenders. Here: c6, then b6, then the a-pawn runs — and the tablebase confirms the order is not interchangeable.

annotations: Queen against king and two crawling pawns: the rest is technique the drill lets you play out. Count this shape once and you will see it for the rest of your chess life.

The point of everything: the a-pawn — the outside file — steps past the wreckage. Two pawns were spent to make this one unstoppable, and the recapture that felt automatic would have rebuilt Black's wall instead. Material is irrelevant; the runner is everything.
The second sacrifice, offered before Black's structure can settle. Declining fails too: the tablebase confirms every Black reply here loses.
The breakthrough starts with the middle pawn. Three abreast against two, and the front is sold, not squeezed: this pawn will not survive, and was never meant to.

checkpoints.label: The front is open a crack — commit or consolidate?
The recapture that rebuilds the wall

deviations.note: The outside pawn first — one move out of order, and the tablebase says the win is gone: the front seals and no runner ever emerges. Same three pawns, same idea, draw. Verified.
The mirror order also breaks through and also wins by tablebase. The drill's line leads with c6 as the standard form; what is not negotiable is that a6 first fails.
Waiting in the corner: verified draw. The breakthrough exists because the kings are far away; every tempo spent not breaking through invites the defender's king back.
The tablebase still says win after this — the breakthrough has not expired — but it improves nothing, and one waiting square (h1) already throws the win away. The break does not age well.
Recapturing rebuilds the wall you just paid a pawn to open: verified draw. The sacrifice's product was the open b-file for the b-pawn, not the material.
A tempo late and the roles reverse: Black's connected pawns and returning king now win — the tablebase calls this LOST, not drawn. The breakthrough is not merely urgent; half-measures lose. Verified.
The automatic recapture, and a verified draw: after it Black's king returns in time. a6! — the pawn that walks PAST the capture — is the only winning move on the board. Verified.
Anything slow here loses outright by tablebase: two Black pawns are already past their blockers. Verified loss.

feedbackClaims.text: At the root, c6 and b6 win and a6 draws; two moves later a6 is the only winning move on the board. Both facts are tablebase-verified. Breakthrough technique is order, not idea.
The winning line gives away two of three pawns. Both recaptures that would keep material even were queried and draw. In breakthrough positions pawn count is fuel spent, not score.

The shape entry this pack drills triggers on an existing wing passer — which appears only at move three of the winning line. The pre-breakthrough position is invisible to the structural vocabulary; recognising it before it exists is exactly the skill being drilled.
Outcome drill: promote and win. The mirror order b6-first is a verified equal win and passes identically.

sources: Start position is the classic three-abreast-versus-two breakthrough schematic (White a5, b5, c5, Kg2; Black a7, b7, Ke6), constructed. The 3v3 version is the more famous textbook diagram; this 3v2 form was chosen because seven pieces sit inside Syzygy range, so every claim of this pack could be machine-checked.

TABLEBASE VERIFIED: root and every position after every spine move queried against Syzygy via tablebase.lichess.org /standard, queried 2026-08-14 (UTC). Root: win (DTZ 1). Root move split verified: c6 and b6 win, a6 and Kh1 draw, king moves win. After 1...bxc6: b6 is the unique win, bxc6 draws, all else loses. After 2...axb6: a6 is the unique win, axb6 draws, all else loses. Every deviation note's category is the queried one.
The Syzygy assessment declaration is NOT ledger-verified (no sourcing sidecars).

SHAPE-TRIGGER HONESTY: content/shapes/pawn-breakthrough-outside-passer.json cannot fire at this root — no passed pawn exists until move three. The entry's own provenance records this exact gap ('the family is wider than the trigger'); the reference here is to what the pack hands off to, not what is detectable at the start.
AUTHORED, NOT PROVED: all prose reasoning, including the 'seals the front' mechanism behind the a6 draw — the tablebase grounds the category, not the explanation.
Move legality: python-chess 1.11.2 at build time; `make pack-check` authoritative.
graduationBlockers: Prose explanations are authored; categories are tablebase-grounded.

The famous 3v3 sibling root (a5b5c5 vs a7b7c7) is eight pieces and outside tablebase range; a pack for it would need the Stockfish authoring substitute of docs/content-sourcing.md and is deliberately not smuggled in here.
